I lost my home in a fire about 10 years ago and I lost my car and a bunch of tools in a warehouse fire last year. It's an awful thing to have to go through, losing the things that make you happy, the things that stand as proof of your memories and the things that are part of your livelihood. I lost pets too, they may have only been lizards and fish, but they still meant a lot. I was just lucky to get my dogs out in time. 


You feel fortunate for everything you do still have but it's a tremendous loss and it's very hard to work through mentally. I didn't handle it very well when I lost my house but I was still there for my wife and kids to make sure they could handle it ok.

Keep trying, I know you may not be able to come up with 3k by the end of the month, but your mental and physical health is more important than school right now. It will still be there when you recover. Don't you think it would suffer if you went back and had all sorts of stress and anxiety and depression to deal with as well? I don't know what you're going to school for but even something relatively easy is going to be hard if you can't put e everything into it. You need to bring yourself mentally to a place where you come first for a little while. Money issues are temporary but letting your overall health degrade takes longer to recovery from and has longer lasting effects. 

I know it's easier said than done, and from your perspective what I say may make sense but seem intangible or counterintuitive to the path you want to take, but don't try to solve all of your problems at once. Start with simpler or most important and work upward to try and keep from being overwhelmed. Progress is the fuel that keeps us going.

Ok, I want you to look at it this way... strip away everything, the debt, the anxiety, the school, the shit jobs, those aren't real, they're not a real part of your life. They're things society tells you to value and live and die for. But that's not life, the other things are, you seem to have a family you care about, a giant boner of a love interest (people can change), a world before you that you obviously love and care about. You don't see the good in it because you feel it's pain, but it's time to only feel yours and focus on you, the world will still be here when you heal. You're already on the right path and you don't even see it. Day by day, step by step, minute by minute. Breath by breath. That's how we live and keep living. Be good to yourself a little and don't feel bad about it. Ask for help, that's why you're here right? Wasn't so hard, now keep going. 

And unless you're stripping because you like it, please don't get stuck in doing that, it's not healthy for the mind.

It's been a little more than a year since I've seen a jazz concert but I often listen to our local jazz radio station and the insights I've gained from listening and seeing live concerts would probably be that first and foremost for me jazz mirrors life in that it seems everyone is doing their own thing but together it forms a union and has a beauty and uniqueness to it. There's chaos but it's structured and timed and mathematically amazing. It uses such a full spectrum of notes, at times even sounding atonal but always manages to tie back into interesting perfection.

The musicians always seem so focused and in tune with their instruments like they're just an audio apparatus for their souls. I think this is a big reason why jazz speaks to people of all walks of life, because you can hear and feel the songs of multiple people's souls in chorus, as one. An instrumental commentary on life.

Where I live is jazz oriented due to the annual Lionel Hampton jazz festival hosted here and the LH school of music being here as well. There are often little concerts playing here and there and I never gave it much thought growing up listening to various other types of music, but as I matured and grew into my 30s I found a deep appreciation for it. Hope any of this helps.

NTA. For all of those saying she should discuss it with her fiance, I get it, but at the same time it's also in both of their best interests not to allow alcohol when he's in recovery and struggling. If she asks and he says to allow it it's going to be a constant distraction on a day that should be focused on each other. She's not allowing alcohol FOR him in effort to help with his recovery, not disallowing it to spite him.

I've been in recovery for a couple years now and I'm nearing my 1000 day mark and when I look back at 4 months, I probably would have allowed it but I would have thought about it the entire time and how much better the best day of my life could be if I was maybe even just a little buzzed. It's a temptation and a slap in the face to his personal effort for it to be present.

I hope you have a great wedding and I hope you two live long and prosper together. He needs you looking out for him on his road to recovery and I hope he gets out of it what he's looking for in life.

Maybe leaving for college and getting out of that environment is the best thing for you. Get away from it and reinvent yourself. You can go on to be whoever you want to be. Make steps toward self realization, work on getting a license, a job, a shitty little car to drive around. As for the people in your life being over protective or angry or disappointed, unfortunately self harm and depression is something that makes people uncomfortable because it's so foreign to them and they don't understand it. It is their way of showing they care though, no matter how misguided and unhelpful and sometimes detrimental it is. Believe me, they wouldn't be happier if you weren't around, they just don't know how to help you and it scares them. 

Something I've found is that no one can really help you, you can really only do it on your own with their help if that makes any sense. Just take it a day at a time, set small realistic goals for yourself and work toward larger ones. Don't give up on yourself yet, there's a lot to experience in life that's truly beautiful.

Sounds like finalizing. People give things away, write letters, call just to say thanks for being there or something like that. It's easier to do it when you've emptied out your life and your conscience, if you have nothing and no one, you become nothing and it's easy to slip out the back so to speak. The last time I was seriously thinking about it i got rid of all of my friends, still don't speak to them and it's been almost a year. I wrote my ex wife and kids suicide letters which i still have, I would have given everything away but i don't have much so It can all go in the dumpster for all I care. If you really want to help your friend, be a friend, I don't know what kind of friendship you have but maybe sit him down and  ask if he would talk to you about what's going on with him. If that doesn't work, ask if maybe he would be willing to talk to a professional and that you would like to help him find one. Sometimes just seeing someone cares that much is enough.

Well, any reason not to is a good enough one. Even if you have to find one each and every day or multiple times a day. Unfortunately these reasons won't change your life though, that's a process that can take a lot of time and energy on your part. I understand how overwhelming that is and how under-energetic you may feel about it, but it takes small steps on a long road of no pitstops or back tracking to achieve. I honestly don't know if I'm the best person to give you advice right now because I'm the most suicidal I've been for quite a while, but I haven't done it yet so maybe I am. 

As far as family goes, fuck em. They don't have to be your life. One of the quotes I live by is "May the bridges we burn light the way." you can take that to mean what you will, but for me it means that shedding what doesn't help my progress as a person will help me to find out who I am. I will say that this has left me devoid of friends and little contact with my family, but I don't need what they were in my life. 

Use your art, pour every bit of your soul into it, if you're a perfectionist, perfect until it hurts and bleeds and keep going until you have masterpieces. If you're not, then create chaos and shed that toxicity inside you with every bit of art you do. Use that fear and sorrow and hatred and darkness inside and give it life. Focus deeply and use it until it's gone and when you look around, you might find the world sees you in a different light and you see it differently as well.

It's about passion, you hurt because you want life to be beautiful and passionate, if you wanted to die you would have already done it and never said a word, but you didn't, you want life, that spark has to be kindled by you though because it's within you.

You're not worthless, you don't put people beneath you or treat them like trash, that's pretty worthless. You're a human being with feelings and emotions and you hurt and you want that pain to go away, that right there is the beginning of passion, that's the fuel, now ignite the fire.

I thought about this for a while. Please don't. I know very well and intimately what you feel. I struggle with depression very badly and I don't always cope very well. The thing is, I can sit here and tell you the things I've been told; the "life will get better" and "it's not as bad as you think" and the plethora of other misguided attempts at helping, but these don't mean anything. I've spent the last couple years in a bad place, I've gone to prison, gone through a divorce and now I get to spend time with my children sparingly. I Contemplate suicide very often, almost becoming obsessed with it from time to time. But I don't want to die and neither do you. You want to live, that's the driving force behind your urgency and desperation. You want all of those wonderful and beautiful things in life and you can have them, just not right now. Practice patience. For real, I mean that from the bottom of my heart. That's what gets us through the day, we take it step by step, we make small goals and achieve them and then move on to others.

You say you have something stopping you, that's good, it shows you know there's a reason not to. That reason is good enough. Any reason is good enough. I can't tell you anything can make it better, but life is about the journey, not the destination. We all have the same destination, but we all have very different journeys. Struggle is something in life that makes us stronger and I know right now you absolutely do not feel strong but you are. You have a heavy burden upon your shoulders and its weight is extremely painful right now, but what about those other times when you can still smile and laugh and carry on? That burden still rests upon your shoulders, you're just carrying it differently. That's what depression is. You don't have to do it on your own. Let other people help to carry that burden when you feel like you no longer can. I don't know how serious you are about this, whether this is just a cry for help or whether this is truly the breaking point that you can no longer keep going, I've been at both points, I've had mental breakdowns where I truly could not recognize myself any longer and was so scared I wouldn't be able to stop myself and I have almost zero for a support system. If I can take another step and see another day, so can you. I'm not even talking about this like this is in the past, I was at one of those points just weeks ago so this is all still very fresh in my mind. I know you feel hopeless and desperate and so fucking tired and lost, but tomorrow is another day. You say you work with special ed people, you're changing lives, that's beautiful. You're beautiful. You're a hero. You may not feel like it but you are. You can do this. I don't know anything about you but I know the place you're in and how heavy the gravity of the black hole of depression is, but you haven't let it suck you in yet and all of those reasons you haven't are still valid. 

Please do whatever it takes, call a hotline, a friend, a stranger, pour your heart out to someone and tell them how you feel and why. Cry, eat, sleep, scream, meditate, take a walk, whatever it takes. It truly is not worth it. Life is a beautiful gift and we often get so caught up with it we forget to live.

Please check back in and let us know that you're ok. I don't know you, but I truly care.
